# Efficiency fixture contract

These fixtures are synthetic test data, not measured productivity evidence.

`transitive-manifest.json` has a deliberately regressed library (zero is treated as unavailable) whose narrow smoke check passes but consumer contract fails; planning only the edited library would miss that failure. Manifest v1 contains `projects` with repository-relative `paths` globs (`*` or `**`), project `dependsOn`, and `checks` IDs. Check definitions contain argument-array `command`, check `dependsOn`, and optional Node platform names. `alwaysRequired` runs regardless of selection; unmapped files select `broadChecks`. Manifests are trusted local executable configuration, not a format to run from untrusted sources.

`synthetic-trials.json` documents trial v1. Match baseline/candidate by `taskId`, `batch`, `heldOut`, and optional string `repetition` (defaults to `1`). Both variants must share `taskType`. Every attempt explicitly records `accepted`, `deterministicPassed`, `failed`, and `retried`. Numeric resource measurements are optional and separate: `latencySeconds`, `tokens`, and `costUsd`. Human measurements are `userOverheadSeconds` and `developerSeconds`; each requires `provenance: {"kind":"human-observation","source":"actual observer record reference"}`. Include unsuccessful and retried attempt time. The dataset must additionally declare `observationKind: "human-observation"` before targets can be computed. Never relabel fixtures as observations.

The report has separate `batches`, explicit `combined` (only `batch: "combined"` trials), `heldOut`, and descriptive `pooled` results. Each comparison reports sample counts, resource distributions, paired changes, outcomes, and `targets`. Targets require complete matched human measurements, valid denominators, non-synthetic data, and preserved quality. Quality-valid accepted work means the final attempt was accepted, passed deterministic checks, and did not fail. User overhead is total observed overhead divided by quality-valid accepted tasks; productivity is quality-valid accepted tasks per total developer-hour. The targets are 15% overhead reduction and 10% productivity increase. The tool reports descriptive results without a statistical significance claim or model adoption recommendation.
